chunks: What Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, that he said:

"Water is to be sought during travel: if the land is rough, then [one searches] the distance of an arrow-shot; and if it is easy, level land, then two arrow-shots. More than that is not to be sought." And this does not contradict [that].

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state in which this ruling applies
key_terms.سَهْمٍ: an arrow, used here as a measure of distance
key_terms.لَا يُطْلَبُ: is not to be sought beyond the stated limit
key_terms.يُطْلَبُ: is to be sought or searched for

ai.seo_question: How far must water be sought during travel before performing tayammum?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the extent to which a traveler must search for water before resorting to tayammum. It specifies different search distances based on whether the terrain is rough or level, indicating a measured obligation in ritual purity during travel.
